setting: A fictional first meeting between neighbours in the entrance of an apartment building.

presentation.situation: You meet Alex, who moved into {{flat}} {{moved}}, in the entrance of your building. Say hello, tell Alex your name, have a short friendly chat, and say goodbye.
presentation.opening: Hi! I'm Alex, your neighbour. I just moved in to {{flat}}. What's your name?

brief.you_are: You live in this building and you are meeting a new neighbour.
brief.situation: Your new neighbour Alex says hello to you in the entrance.
brief.task: Say hello, tell Alex your name, ask or answer one friendly question, then say goodbye.
brief.done_looks_like: Alex knows your name, you had a short friendly chat, and you said goodbye politely.

participants.name: You
goals: Greet Alex, share your name and close politely

card.want: Get to know one friendly person in the new building and find out where the nearest shop is.
card.hidden_need: Feels a little lonely after the move.
card.attitude: Warm, patient, happy to chat for a minute.
card.speech: Very simple everyday English. Short sentences. One easy question at a time.
tactics: Use the learner's name once you know it
If the learner gives a very short answer, ask one easy question

pressure.challenging: Friendly, normal pace, slightly longer sentences.

ledger.text: Alex is looking for the nearest food shop and does not know the area yet.
Alex has to leave soon to {{errand}}.

objectives.evidence: The learner says hello or an equivalent greeting to Alex.
The learner tells Alex their own name.
The learner ends the chat with a goodbye or an equivalent polite closing.

opportunity: Sorry, I didn't get your name. What is your name?
beats.orient: We are neighbours and we are just saying hello. I'm Alex. Please tell me your name.
fallback: Nice to meet you. What's your name?
Hello! I'm happy to meet you.

beats.goal: Have a short friendly chat about the building or the area.
opportunity: Is there a food shop near here?
What do you do for work?
beats.orient: We are just having a short chat. You can tell me about the area. Is there a food shop near here?
fallback: Is there a food shop near here?
I like this building. Do you like it here?

beats.goal: End the chat politely because Alex has to leave.
opportunity: Oh, I have to {{errand}} now. It was nice to meet you!
I really must go now. See you later?
beats.orient: I have to go now, so we are saying goodbye. You can say: goodbye, see you soon.
fallback: I have to go now. It was nice to meet you!

closing_line: Thank you. See you around the building!

o1.good: A short greeting that matches the moment, such as Hi or Good morning, before anything else.
common_mistakes: Answering the question without any greeting
o1.micro_lesson: Start with a small greeting. Just 'Hi' is friendly and enough.
o1.smaller_step: Say just one word of greeting to Alex.

o2.good: Saying your own name in a full short sentence so the other person can use it.
common_mistakes: Giving only the name with no sentence is fine, but some learners forget to answer the question at all
o2.micro_lesson: When someone asks your name, use: My name is, or I'm, then your name.
o2.model: I'm Sara. Nice to meet you.
o2.smaller_step: Say: My name is, and then your own name.

o3.good: A polite closing when the other person has to leave.
o3.micro_lesson: When someone says they have to go, answer with a goodbye so the chat ends warmly.
o3.model: Nice to meet you too. See you soon!
